blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Section 8 focuses on basic linear seating arrangement problem-solving techniques.
Section 9 covers logical statements, specifically examining Cause–Effect relationships and Assertion-Type questions.
An Answer Key is provided to verify solutions and track performance accuracy.

Concept:

Seating arrangement questions test the ability to arrange persons according to given conditions. In SSC, seating arrangement questions are usually linear, simple and direct.

Types Common in SSC:

• Persons sitting in a row

• Facing north or south

• Simple left–right or middle positions

Method to Solve:

1. Fix the direction of the row first.

2. Place the sure information such as middle or end positions.

3. Use remaining conditions step-by-step.

4. Avoid jumping to conclusions early.
A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row.
A is to the left of C.
B is to the right of C.

Logic:

There are five persons, so the middle position is third.

C occupies the middle.

A is placed to the left of C.

B is placed to the right of C.

One end is occupied by D, so the other end must be E.



Answer: E

blocks.content:
Practice Questions (Seating Arrangement):

Q1. P, Q, R and S are sitting in a row facing north.

R is to the right of Q.

P is to the left of Q.



Who is sitting at the left end?

A. P B. Q C. R D. S



Q2. Five persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row.

B is between A and C.

D is at one end.

E is to the right of C.



Who is sitting in the middle?

A. A B. B C. C D. E

items:
Concept:

Logical statement questions test the ability to understand cause–effect relationships or draw conclusions based strictly on the given statement.

Common Question Types:

• Cause and effect

• Statement–Conclusion

• Course of action (basic)

Method to Solve:

1. Read the statement carefully.

2. Identify the cause and the result.

3. Do not use outside knowledge.

4. Select the option that logically follows.

blocks.content:
Solved Example:

Statement:

The government increased fuel prices.

Conclusion:

Transport cost may increase.

Logic:

Increase in fuel prices directly affects transport costs.



Answer: Conclusion follows.

Practice Questions (Logical Statements):

Q3. Statement:

Heavy rainfall has damaged crops in many areas.

Conclusion:

Food prices may rise.



A. Conclusion follows

items: Linear Seating Arrangement questions frequently appear in SSC exams to test positional logic and row orientation.
Assertion and Cause-Effect questions test analytical reasoning by evaluating whether one statement directly determines or explains another.
